1	# The Global Burden of Mental Illness: Prevalence, Impact, and the Treatment Gap
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	
     5	Our World in Data — Mental Health  
     6	URL: https://ourworldindata.org/mental-health  
     7	Authors: Saloni Dattani, Lucas Rodés-Guirao, Hannah Ritchie, and Max Roser (2023)  
     8	Data source: IHME, Global Burden of Disease (2025)
     9	
    10	## Overview: Why Mental Health Matters
    11	
    12	Mental health is an essential part of people's lives and society. Poor mental health affects well-being, the ability to work, and relationships with friends, family, and community. Hundreds of millions of people suffer from mental health conditions each year, and many more experience them over their lifetimes.
    13	
    14	Key prevalence estimates:
    15	- **1 in 3 women** will experience major depression in their lifetime.
    16	- **1 in 5 men** will experience major depression in their lifetime.
    17	- Other conditions such as schizophrenia and bipolar disorder are less common but have a large impact on individuals' lives.
    18	
    19	Mental illnesses are treatable and their impact can be reduced. Despite this, treatment is often lacking or of poor quality. Many people feel uncomfortable sharing their symptoms with healthcare professionals or people they know, which also makes it difficult to estimate the actual prevalence of mental illnesses.
    20	
    21	## Disease Burden by Category of Mental Illness (World, 2023)
    22	
    23	The burden of disease is measured in disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) per 100,000 people. DALYs combine years of life lost due to premature death and years lived with disability, providing a comprehensive measure of overall disease impact.
    24	
    25	| Mental Illness Category | DALYs per 100,000 people |
    26	|---|---|
    27	| Depressive disorders | 694.6 |
    28	| Anxiety disorders | 686.5 |
    29	| Schizophrenia | 210.2 |
    30	| Bipolar disorder | 94.6 |
    31	| Eating disorders | 47.5 |
    32	
    33	![Burden of disease from each category of mental illness, World, 2023](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    34	
    35	Depressive disorders and anxiety disorders together dominate the global mental health burden, with nearly identical DALY rates (~695 and ~687 respectively). Combined, they account for roughly 80% of the total mental health disease burden across these five categories. Schizophrenia, while affecting fewer people, still contributes 210.2 DALYs per 100,000 — reflecting the severe disability associated with the condition. Bipolar disorder and eating disorders contribute smaller but meaningful shares.
    36	
    37	## How People Cope with Mental Health Conditions
    38	
    39	Global survey data reveals wide variation in how people deal with anxiety or depression:
    40	
    41	- **Taking prescribed medication** — common in higher-income settings
    42	- **Engaging in religious or spiritual activities** — prevalent in many regions worldwide
    43	- **Talking to friends or family** — a widely reported coping mechanism
    44	
    45	![Coping strategies across countries](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    46	
    47	The diversity of coping strategies underscores that mental health responses are shaped by cultural, economic, and healthcare system factors. Policy interventions must account for these differences rather than applying a one-size-fits-all approach.
    48	
    49	## The Treatment Gap and Data Challenges
    50	
    51	Despite the availability of effective treatments, significant barriers persist:
    52	
    53	- **Stigma**: Many people are uncomfortable disclosing symptoms to healthcare professionals or even to people they know.
    54	- **Access**: Treatment is often lacking, especially in low- and middle-income countries.
    55	- **Quality**: Even where treatment exists, it may be of poor quality.
    56	- **Underreporting**: Discomfort with disclosure makes it difficult to estimate the true prevalence of mental illnesses, meaning the actual burden may be higher than reported figures suggest.
    57	
    58	Good data is essential to understand these conditions — how, when, and why they occur, how many people are affected, and how they can be treated effectively and safely.
    59	
    60	## Key Findings
    61	
    62	- **Depression and anxiety are the dominant contributors** to the global mental health disease burden, each generating approximately 690 DALYs per 100,000 people — nearly equal in magnitude.
    63	- **Schizophrenia carries a disproportionately high individual burden** relative to its prevalence, contributing 210.2 DALYs per 100,000.
    64	- **Lifetime depression risk is substantial**: 1 in 3 women and 1 in 5 men will experience major depression.
    65	- **A large treatment gap persists** due to stigma, poor access, and inadequate quality of care, meaning the true burden is likely underestimated.
    66	- **Coping strategies vary widely** across countries and cultures, from medication to spiritual practices to social support, highlighting the need for culturally sensitive policy responses.

    51	
    52	# PPTX Manipulation Skill
    53	
    54	## Overview
    55	
    56	This skill enables programmatic creation, editing, and manipulation of Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx) presentations using the **python-pptx** library. Create professional slides with text, shapes, images, charts, and tables without manual editing.
    57	
    58	## How to Use
    59	
    60	1. Describe the presentation you want to create or modify
    61	2. Provide content, data, or images to include
    62	3. I'll generate python-pptx code and execute it
    63	
    64	**Example prompts:**
    65	- "Create a 10-slide pitch deck from this outline"
    66	- "Add a chart to slide 3 with this data"
    67	- "Extract all text from this presentation"
    68	- "Generate slides from this markdown content"
    69	
    70	## Domain Knowledge
    71	
    72	### python-pptx Fundamentals
    73	
    74	```python
    75	from pptx import Presentation
    76	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
    77	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
    78	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
    79	
    80	# Create new presentation
    81	prs = Presentation()
    82	
    83	# Or open existing
    84	prs = Presentation('existing.pptx')
    85	```
    86	
    87	### Presentation Structure
    88	```
    89	Presentation
    90	├── slide_layouts (predefined layouts)
    91	├── slides (individual slides)
    92	│   ├── shapes (text, images, charts)
    93	│   │   ├── text_frame (paragraphs)
    94	│   │   └── table (rows, cells)
    95	│   └── placeholders (title, content)
    96	└── slide_masters (templates)
    97	```
    98	
    99	### Slide Layouts
   100	```python
   101	# Common layout indices (may vary by template)
   102	TITLE_SLIDE = 0
   103	TITLE_CONTENT = 1
   104	SECTION_HEADER = 2
   105	TWO_CONTENT = 3
   106	COMPARISON = 4
   107	TITLE_ONLY = 5
   108	BLANK = 6
   109	
   110	# Add slide with layout
   111	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[TITLE_CONTENT]
   112	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   113	```
   114	
   115	### Adding Content
   116	
   117	#### Title Slide
   118	```python
   119	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0]  # Title slide
   120	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   121	
   122	title = slide.shapes.title
   123	subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]
   124	
   125	title.text = "Quarterly Report"
   126	subtitle.text = "Q4 2024 Performance Review"
   127	```
   128	
   129	#### Text Content
   130	```python
   131	# Using placeholder
   132	body = slide.placeholders[1]
   133	tf = body.text_frame
   134	tf.text = "First bullet point"
   135	
   136	# Add more paragraphs
   137	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   138	p.text = "Second bullet point"
   139	p.level = 0
   140	
   141	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   142	p.text = "Sub-bullet"
   143	p.level = 1
   144	```
   145	
   146	#### Text Box
   147	```python
   148	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   149	
   150	left = Inches(1)
   151	top = Inches(2)
   152	width = Inches(4)
   153	height = Inches(1)
   154	
   155	txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
   156	tf = txBox.text_frame
   157	
   158	p = tf.paragraphs[0]
   159	p.text = "Custom text box"
   160	p.font.bold = True
   161	p.font.size = Pt(18)
   162	```
   163	
   164	#### Shapes
   165	```python
   166	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
   167	
   168	# Rectangle
   169	shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
   170	    MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
   171	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # left, top
   172	    Inches(3), Inches(1.5) # width, height
   173	)
   174	shape.text = "Rectangle with text"
   175	
   176	# Common shapes:
   177	# MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   178	# MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, CHEVRON, ARROW_RIGHT
   179	# MSO_SHAPE.CALLOUT_ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   180	```
   181	
   182	#### Images
   183	```python
   184	# Add image
   185	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   186	    'image.png',
   187	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # position
   188	    width=Inches(4)        # auto height
   189	)
   190	
   191	# Or specify both dimensions
   192	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   193	    'logo.png',
   194	    Inches(8), Inches(0.5),
   195	    Inches(1.5), Inches(0.75)
   196	)
   197	```
   198	
   199	### Tables
   200	```python
   201	# Create table
   202	rows, cols = 4, 3
   203	left = Inches(1)
   204	top = Inches(2)
   205	width = Inches(8)
   206	height = Inches(2)
   207	
   208	table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height).table
   209	
   210	# Set column widths
   211	table.columns[0].width = Inches(2)
   212	table.columns[1].width = Inches(3)
   213	table.columns[2].width = Inches(3)
   214	
   215	# Add headers
   216	headers = ['Product', 'Q3 Sales', 'Q4 Sales']
   217	for i, header in enumerate(headers):
   218	    cell = table.cell(0, i)
   219	    cell.text = header
   220	    cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
   221	
   222	# Add data
   223	data = [
   224	    ['Widget A', '$10,000', '$12,500'],
   225	    ['Widget B', '$8,000', '$9,200'],
   226	    ['Widget C', '$15,000', '$18,000'],
   227	]
   228	for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data, 1):
   229	    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row_data):
   230	        table.cell(row_idx, col_idx).text = value
   231	```
   232	
   233	### Charts
   234	```python
   235	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   236	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   237	
   238	# Chart data
   239	chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   240	chart_data.categories = ['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4']
   241	chart_data.add_series('Sales', (19.2, 21.4, 16.7, 23.8))
   242	chart_data.add_series('Expenses', (12.1, 15.3, 14.2, 18.1))
   243	
   244	# Add chart
   245	x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1), Inches(2), Inches(8), Inches(4)
   246	chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   247	    XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED,
   248	    x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
   249	).chart
   250	
   251	# Customize
   252	chart.has_legend = True
   253	chart.legend.include_in_layout = False
   254	```
   255	
   256	### Formatting
   257	
   258	#### Text Formatting
   259	```python
   260	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   261	
   262	run = p.runs[0]
   263	run.font.name = 'Arial'
   264	run.font.size = Pt(24)
   265	run.font.bold = True
   266	run.font.italic = True
   267	run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x66, 0xCC)
   268	```
   269	
   270	#### Shape Fill & Line
   271	```python
   272	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   273	
   274	shape.fill.solid()
   275	shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x80, 0x00)
   276	
   277	shape.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
   278	shape.line.width = Pt(2)
   279	```
   280	
   281	#### Paragraph Alignment
   282	```python
   283	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
   284	
   285	p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER  # LEFT, RIGHT, JUSTIFY
   286	```
   287	
   288	## Best Practices
   289	
   290	1. **Use Templates**: Start with a .pptx template for consistent branding
   291	2. **Layout First**: Plan slide structure before coding
   292	3. **Reuse Slide Masters**: Maintain consistency across presentations
   293	4. **Optimize Images**: Compress images before adding
   294	5. **Test Output**: Always verify generated presentations
   295	
   296	## Common Patterns
   297	
   298	### Slide Deck Generator
   299	```python
   300	def create_deck(title, slides_content):
   301	    prs = Presentation()
   302	    
   303	    # Title slide
   304	    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   305	    slide.shapes.title.text = title
   306	    
   307	    # Content slides
   308	    for slide_data in slides_content:
   309	        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   310	        slide.shapes.title.text = slide_data['title']
   311	        
   312	        body = slide.placeholders[1]
   313	        tf = body.text_frame
   314	        for i, point in enumerate(slide_data['points']):
   315	            if i == 0:
   316	                tf.text = point
   317	            else:
   318	                p = tf.add_paragraph()
   319	                p.text = point
   320	    
   321	    return prs
   322	```
   323	
   324	### Data-Driven Charts
   325	```python
   326	def add_bar_chart(slide, title, categories, values):
   327	    from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   328	    from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   329	    
   330	    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   331	    chart_data.categories = categories
   332	    chart_data.add_series('Values', values)
   333	    
   334	    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   335	        XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED,
   336	        Inches(1), Inches(2),
   337	        Inches(8), Inches(4),
   338	        chart_data
   339	    ).chart
   340	    
   341	    chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = title
   342	    return chart
   343	```
   344	
   345	## Examples
   346	
   347	### Example 1: Create a Pitch Deck
   348	```python
   349	from pptx import Presentation
   350	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   351	
   352	prs = Presentation()
   353	
   354	# Slide 1: Title
   355	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   356	slide.shapes.title.text = "StartupX"
   357	slide.placeholders[1].text = "Revolutionizing Document Processing"
   358	
   359	# Slide 2: Problem
   360	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   361	slide.shapes.title.text = "The Problem"
   362	body = slide.placeholders[1].text_frame
   363	body.text = "Manual document processing costs businesses $1T annually"
   364	p = body.add_paragraph()
   365	p.text = "Average worker spends 20% of time on document tasks"
   366	p.level = 1
   367	
   368	# Slide 3: Solution
   369	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   370	slide.shapes.title.text = "Our Solution"
   371	body = slide.placeholders[1].text_frame
   372	body.text = "AI-powered document automation"
   373	body.add_paragraph().text = "90% faster processing"
   374	body.add_paragraph().text = "99.5% accuracy"
   375	body.add_paragraph().text = "Works with existing tools"
   376	
   377	# Slide 4: Market
   378	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])  # Title only
   379	slide.shapes.title.text = "Market Opportunity: $50B by 2028"
   380	
   381	# Add chart
   382	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   383	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   384	
   385	data = CategoryChartData()
   386	data.categories = ['2024', '2025', '2026', '2027', '2028']
   387	data.add_series('Market Size ($B)', [30, 35, 40, 45, 50])
   388	
   389	slide.shapes.add_chart(
   390	    XL_CHART_TYPE.LINE,
   391	    Inches(1), Inches(1.5),
   392	    Inches(8), Inches(5),
   393	    data
   394	)
   395	
   396	prs.save('pitch_deck.pptx')
   397	```
   398	
   399	### Example 2: Report with Data Table
   400	```python
   401	from pptx import Presentation
   402	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   403	
   404	prs = Presentation()
   405	
   406	# Title slide
   407	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   408	slide.shapes.title.text = "Sales Performance Report"
   409	slide.placeholders[1].text = "Q4 2024"
   410	
   411	# Data slide
   412	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])
   413	slide.shapes.title.text = "Regional Performance"
   414	
   415	# Create table
   416	table = slide.shapes.add_table(5, 4, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.5), Inches(9), Inches(4)).table
   417	
   418	# Headers
   419	headers = ['Region', 'Revenue', 'Growth', 'Target']
   420	for i, h in enumerate(headers):
   421	    table.cell(0, i).text = h
   422	    table.cell(0, i).text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
   423	
   424	# Data
   425	data = [
   426	    ['North America', '$5.2M', '+15%', 'Met'],
   427	    ['Europe', '$3.8M', '+12%', 'Met'],
   428	    ['Asia Pacific', '$2.9M', '+28%', 'Exceeded'],
   429	    ['Latin America', '$1.1M', '+8%', 'Below'],
   430	]
   431	for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data, 1):
   432	    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row_data):
   433	        table.cell(row_idx, col_idx).text = value
   434	
   435	prs.save('sales_report.pptx')
   436	```

def set_slide_bg_color(slide, color):
    """Set solid background color for a slide."""
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=Pt(14), font_color=COLOR_DARK, bold=False, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name=FONT_BODY):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.color.rgb = font_color
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return txBox

def add_bullet_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets, font_size=Pt(16), font_color=COLOR_DARK, bold=False, font_name=FONT_BODY):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, text in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = text
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.color.rgb = font_color
        p.font.bold = bold
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.level = 0
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
    return txBox

    p.font.name = FONT_HEADING
    p2 = tf.add_paragraph()
    p2.text = "\n" + desc
    p2.font.size = Pt(16)
    p2.font.color.rgb = COLOR_DARK
    p2.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
    p2.font.name = FONT_BODY

# Bottom note
note = (
    "The diversity of coping strategies underscores that mental health responses are shaped by cultural, economic, and healthcare system factors. "
    "Policy interventions must account for these differences rather than applying a one-size-fits-all approach."
)
add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(4.8), Inches(11.7), Inches(1.0), note,
            font_size=Pt(16), font_color=COLOR_DARK)

add_footer(slide)
add_slide_number(slide, 6)

# ============================================================
# Slide 8 — Takeaways and Implications
# ============================================================
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_bg_color(slide, COLOR_BG)

add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.35), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.9),
            "Key Takeaways: Prioritizing Depression, Anxiety, and Closing the Treatment Gap",
            font_size=Pt(28), font_color=COLOR_PRIMARY, bold=True)

bullets = [
    "1. Depression and anxiety together represent the overwhelming majority of mental health DALYs — policy should treat them as co-equal priorities.",
    "2. Schizophrenia and bipolar disorder carry disproportionate individual burden; specialized care must be maintained even as common-disorder services scale.",
    "3. Effective treatments exist, but access and quality remain inadequate — especially in low- and middle-income countries.",
    "4. Stigma suppresses both help-seeking and accurate data; reducing it is a prerequisite for closing the treatment gap.",
    "5. Policy should prioritize scaling evidence-based interventions for common mental disorders while maintaining specialized care for severe conditions.",
]

add_bullet_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.4), Inches(11.7), Inches(4.8), bullets,
                   font_size=Pt(20), font_color=COLOR_DARK)

# Closing badge
close = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, Inches(0.8), Inches(6.2), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.7))
close.fill.solid()
close.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_PRIMARY
close.line.fill.background()
tf_c = close.text_frame
tf_c.word_wrap = True
p = tf_c.paragraphs[0]
p.text = "Evidence-based, culturally informed, and equitably distributed mental health care is both achievable and urgently needed."
p.font.size = Pt(18)
p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_WHITE
p.font.bold = True
p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
p.font.name = FONT_HEADING

add_footer(slide)
add_slide_number(slide, 7)

# ============================================================
# Save
# ============================================================
output_path = "/app/output/final_deck.pptx"
prs.save(output_path)
print(f"Saved to {output_path}")
